title: EmberGlow platform onboarding immersion kickoff
summary: Kickoff for EmberGlow's Redwood onboarding. Covered architecture choices (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements (SOC 2 / KMS / SSO), initial integration plan and timings. Agreed to run a short token-cost benchmark and provide security pack. Action items and next steps captured.
next_steps: Redwood to send security compliance pack (SOC2, ISO) by 2026-06-10
SE to schedule a 1-hour performance benchmark run by 2026-06-15
Customer to share sample inference workload and token distribution by 2026-06-12
Schedule canary rollout planning session wk of 6/22
action_items: Maya Chen - Send security & deployment docs - due 2026-06-10
Ravi Patel - Prepare perf test plan and empty benchmark script - due 2026-06-11
Tomás Ruiz - Share sample payloads and expected QPS - due 2026-06-12
Sana Ahmed - Provide compliance contact and KMS requirements - due 2026-06-10
header:
Date: 2026-06-08
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM); Julia Park, Darren Lee, Sana Ahmed, Tomás Ruiz (EmberGlow)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood Inference. real quick, intro round.
[00:12] Julia Park: Hi, Julia here, I'm Head of MLOps at EmberGlow. We're running a mix of batch and near-real-time scoring right now.
[00:22] Darren Lee: Darren - VP Eng. We're focused on reliability and cost, big on audit trails.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Great. Ravi, quick intro?
[00:33] Ravi Patel: Hey all, Ravi, SE. I'll be leading the perf scoping and integrations. Quick note - we saw the sample architecture doc you sent, looks like you have a self-hosted model for face/lab reports?
[00:45] Tomás Ruiz: Yeah, Tomas. We have a fine-tuned Llama variant for clinical summarization, plus some proprietary models. We're trying to move away from running everything locally because cost is spiking.
[00:58] Maya Chen: Cool. Today's agenda — deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security controls, pilot definition, and timeline. Anything to add?
[01:07] Sana Ahmed: I want to make sure we cover key management — HSM or customer-managed KMS — and audit logs for regulators. Also SSO and RBAC.
[01:15] Lena Ortiz: From onboarding side I'll capture runbook expectations and support SLAs.
[01:22] Maya Chen: Awesome. So first, deployment constraints. Can you describe network and data residency needs?
[01:30] Julia Park: We're US-only for PHI, so data can't leave region. We have an internal VPC and strict egress rules.
[01:37] Ravi Patel: Okay, so Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering would fit. Note: our Private offering gives a customer-managed control plane option and can be air-gapped if needed.
[01:48] Darren Lee: What's the difference in latency and ops between Dedicated and Private? We need <200ms p95 on short summaries.
[01:56] Ravi Patel: Good question. Dedicated on Redwood infra typically gives the best balance — managed control plane, reserved GPUs for predictable latency. Private can match latency but requires more infra ownership from your side. There's also some overhead for on-prem networking and KV-cache warmups.
[02:10] Tomás Ruiz: You mentioned KV cache — do you mean the key value cache for long-running chat? We mostly do short prompts but reuse prefixes.
[02:18] Ravi Patel: Yes, KV cache / prefix caching helps cut token cost and latency for repeated prefixes. We'll profile your token distribution as part of the perf test.
[02:27] Maya Chen: Let's talk security briefly. Sana, can you list the minimum compliance items we need from Redwood?
[02:35] Sana Ahmed: SOC two report, ISO attestation, encryption at rest with our KMS, TLS in transit, full audit logs with retention controls, and SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning ideally. Also, need to understand data retention — do you buffer prompts?
[02:48] Ravi Patel: By default hosted API retains short-term logs for debugging; Dedicated and Private can be configured to disable retention. We'll include our data residency and retention options in the pack.
[02:59] Jana— sorry, Julia: If we go dedicated, do we still get console observability?
[03:05] Lena Ortiz: Yes, Dedicated gets Console dashboards, token-cost breakdowns, per-route tracing and can integrate with your SIEM.
[03:12] Darren Lee: On the cost side, is quantization supported to reduce GPU requirements? We looked at 4-bit quantization to cut footprint.
[03:20] Ravi Patel: We support quantization profiles; Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization + batching configs based on your sequences. For clinical accuracy we'll run evals to ensure quality doesn't degrade.
[03:32] Tomás Ruiz: Great. For the pilot, here's what we had in mind: 10k daily requests, 30 QPS bursts, avg prompt length 120 tokens, mostly deterministic outputs.
[03:43] Ravi Patel: That helps. We'll set up a bench with those QPS and token distributions. Plan is to run 3 scenarios: baseline hosted, dedicated with reserved capacity, and private minimal infra to compare p95 latency and tokens per second.
[03:56] Maya Chen: Timeline — quick proposal: security pack by Wed (6/10), perf plan and script by Thu (6/11), customer payloads by Fri (6/12), run bench next week (6/15-6/18), then a results review 6/19. Thoughts?
[04:12] Darren Lee: That timeline works if you hit those dates. We need pricing ballpark before the bench though so procurement has context.
[04:20] Maya Chen: We'll include estimated unit economics in the pack — hosted and dedicated TCO vs private ops.
[04:26] Sana Ahmed: One concern — SSO and SCIM will require an Okta integration. How long does that take?
[04:32] Ravi Patel: Okta SAML + SCIM provisioning usually 2-3 days to configure end-to-end if you can provide metadata and a test user. We'll capture the required artifacts in the security checklist.
[04:42] Tomás Ruiz: On telemetry — we want token-level costs and request-level trace IDs forwarded to our Splunk. Is that supported?
[04:49] Lena Ortiz: Yes, we can forward traces via webhook or push to a SIEM endpoint. We'll capture the event schema; might be slightly different in Private but we can match fields.
[04:59] Julia Park: A couple of red flags from our side: (1) can't have prompts stored unencrypted, (2) need SSO before prod, (3) want rollback playbook for model regression.
[05:12] Ravi Patel: Understood. For (1) we'll lock down retention and show encryption key usage. For (3) Redwood supports canary rollouts, automatic fallback to previous model variant and anomaly alerts tied to eval sets.
[05:24] Darren Lee: What about incident response — who is on-call and SLA for Dedicated?
[05:30] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and prioritized incident response. We'll include the support playbook.
[05:37] Sana Ahmed: Please include details about audit logs retention windows and searchability for compliance investigations.
[05:42] Ravi Patel: We'll include an example retention matrix and log export options.
[05:48] Maya Chen: Ok, let's do a quick recap and next steps — Ravi, you own the perf plan; Maya will send security docs; Tomás and Julia will share workload artifacts; Sana will provide compliance contacts. We'll reconvene after the benchmark with results.
[06:05] Julia Park: Thanks, appreciate the thoroughness.
[06:08] Darren Lee: Thanks all.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — action items in the doc, we'll email follow-up. Bye.
[06:15] (call ends)

Notes on transcript: occasional mis-hearings: 'SOC two' recorded instead of 'SOC 2', 'V P C' sometimes transcribed as 'VPC' or 'V-P-C', 'KV cache' noted as 'key value cache' in places, some filler words and overlaps removed for readability.
